top_choice_rationale: Can Xue (P002) remains my first choice on the common criteria. Her voice is among the most recognizable on the shortlist. Her break with realist psychology, space and causality is the most complete among the candidates. The project has been sustained for several decades in Chinese, with a clean single-writer attribution, and a citation can cover the whole body of work rather than one title. My main reservation is unresolved: I cannot show from public knowledge, or from a partly translated corpus, that the later novels such as Frontier and Love in the New Millennium deepen the method rather than enlarge it. This is a limit on my evidence, not a finding about her merit. I apply the same translation standard to every candidate and have not verified any source. If the committee requires demonstrable development, Cărtărescu (P001) is the better-evidenced alternative, so he is my second choice. Zurita (P003), now with a poems-only citation, is third. Michon (P004) is fourth: his sentence-level achievement is outstanding, but his compact corpus and narrow range fit the whole-oeuvre standard less well. No award (P000) is last, because several candidates have serious claims.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. No documented tie to any proposed laureate. Disclosed as context only: my recorded statements that the Academy has missed many significant women's authorships, and my intent to search the literary world map systematically (the latter reported from an unverified interview summary). Can Xue is a woman writing in Chinese, and I do not treat gender, language or geography as literary merit. Ordinary collegial ties to the other members, including the 2019 renewal round with Mattson. My own novelistic practice is not evidence for any candidate.
